query: How do I make Ham and Cheese Roll-Ups?

goal.title: Make cheese rolls filled with deli meat
goal.description: Unpack cheese and deli meat, cut the meat into strips and roll it inside two cheese slices. Plate both rolls and carry them to the nearby table.
goal.final_state: Two cheese-wrapped meat rolls remain on a white rectangular plate held above the table. No heating or eating is shown.

procedure.description: Approach the counter and move the empty white rectangular plate to the left of the cutting board. Pick up the teal cheese package, open it and remove the stacked slices. Peel off the white separator papers, lay two cheese slices on the board and put the papers beside the package.

Pull back the film on the deli meat package, lift out the thin pale slices and move the package beside the sink. Separate and lay the meat on the cutting board, moving the cheese out of the cutting area.

Take the long knife from the countertop knife block. Hold the meat with the left fingertips and slice it lengthwise into narrow strips using the right hand. Pull the cut strips apart and align them near the upper edge of the board while retaining the knife.

Move a cheese slice into the clear lower part of the board and put the knife down beside the sink. Curl the cheese edge, open it again, pick up and fold meat strips and place them along the edge. Add another strip, roll the cheese around the meat and transfer the first completed roll to the plate.

Move the second cheese slice into position, add folded meat strips along its edge and begin rolling. Retrieve further strips in several passes and tuck them into the developing roll. Continue curling and pressing the cheese until it forms a cylinder, then place the second roll on the plate.

Lift the plate with both hands and carry it from the counter to the nearby table. After the last annotated step at 112.5s, continue holding it above the table. Around 115.8–120.8s the right fingertips lift and reposition one roll on the plate, then release it while the left hand retains the plate. Both rolls remain visible at the end; no eating or heating is shown.

notes: All 31 source fine intervals preserved. Original task wording suggests ham, but the pale packaged deli meat is described neutrally without assuming species. Outer layer is visibly cheese, not meat. Every overview, all 40 dense interval sheets and 31 native end frames inspected; time burned before sampling. Cut strips are sometimes adjusted while knife remains in right hand. Brief cheese contact used for supported rolling is held, whereas touching fixed counter is not. Source fine stops at 112.5s, leaving 11.5s uncovered: t=112.5–115.7s hold plate above table; t=115.8–120.8s right fingertips lift/reposition a roll; t=121.1–124s left hand holds plate with both rolls. Tail dense sheets reviewed and no extra fine segment added. Predictability pending independent blind stage.
